title: Knowledge check: Reporting and Analytics APIs

questions.prompt: How should a team choose a specialized API pattern?
options: Choose the newest pattern regardless of existing consumers or skill constraints.
Replace every REST resource with an RPC endpoint to reduce documentation.
Use a single communication pattern for every workload without reviewing trade-offs.
Compare client needs, domain workflow, payload shape, coupling, latency, security, and operational cost.
questions.answer_key: Compare client needs, domain workflow, payload shape, coupling, latency, security, and operational cost.
questions.explanation: Compare client needs, domain workflow, payload shape, coupling, latency, security, and operational cost. This is especially relevant to “Reporting and Analytics APIs” because the API contract must remain explicit and reviewable.

questions.prompt: For the lesson “Reporting and Analytics APIs”, which check provides the strongest practical evidence?
options: Run one happy-path call and skip invalid, denied, and failure scenarios.
Test against production records so the exercise cannot be repeated safely.
Compare a documented pattern choice with the requirements and test its key trade-offs.
Rely on a code review comment without running any representative check.
questions.answer_key: Compare a documented pattern choice with the requirements and test its key trade-offs.
questions.explanation: A useful check is repeatable, tied to an observable contract, and includes an important negative or boundary scenario.

questions.prompt: Which review warning is most relevant to “Reporting and Analytics APIs”?
options: The API avoids exposing internal secrets and personal data.
A pattern is selected with no requirements or analysis of coupling and operations.
The expected behavior and relevant failure cases are documented.
A representative test can reproduce the result.
questions.answer_key: A pattern is selected with no requirements or analysis of coupling and operations.
questions.explanation: This finding weakens a core API guarantee and should be treated as a design or release issue, not only a style concern.
